docs.text: HardFOC driver SE050 Driver ¶ A C++17 driver for the NXP EdgeLock SE050 secure element. It brings up the T=1 over I2C link, selects the IoT applet and sends its commands: random numbers, secure objects, on-chip EC key generation, ECDSA signing and verification, AES, and an optional GlobalPlatform SCP03 channel, on any MCU with I2C. Quickstart API guide Source on GitHub The driver has no platform code. You give it a small class that writes and reads bytes on I2C and, if your board wires it, drives the SE050's ENA pin; it does the rest: T=1 framing and CRC, chaining, waiting-time extensions, APDU and TLV encoding, and the SCP03 wrap. It allocates nothing and contains no keys. Plug & Trust secure element SE050 NXP Semiconductors (EdgeLock) Function Key storage and crypto: ECC (NIST P-192 to P-521, Brainpool, Curve25519), RSA, AES, SHA-1 and SHA-2, HMAC, TRNG Host interface I2C target, address 0x48, T=1 over I2C (UM11225); up to 1 MHz, 3.4 MHz with clock stretching Supply VIN, VCC 1.62 V to 3.6 V (1.8 V typical); 6 V absolute maximum Memory and security Up to 50 kB user flash; CC EAL 6+; SCP03 bus encryption Package and range HX2QFN20, 3 mm × 3 mm; −25 °C to 85 °C or −40 °C to 105 °C by part number Driver uses The IoT applet over plaintext T=1, or over a platform SCP03 channel with keys you provision Datasheet (NXP) · APDU specification AN12413 · Errata sheet What you get ¶ One object per chip. se050::Device<YourI2c> exposes the applet's commands: GetRandom , WriteBinary , ReadObject , GenerateEcKeyPair , EcdsaSign , EcdsaVerify , CipherAesEcb and more. See the API guide . The link layer handled. T1Session frames blocks, checks the CRC-16, chains in both directions and answers WTX and resynchronisation requests. See T=1 over I2C . Keys stay in the chip. Key pairs are generated inside the SE050; the host only ever sees public keys and signatures. See Security model . SCP03 without default keys. The secure channel opens only with keys you supply at run time; the driver ships no NXP default keys. See Security model . Zero-overhead portability. The port is a CRTP class: no virtual calls, no heap, no RTOS dependency. See Porting . Tested without hardware. Host unit tests run the driver against a model of the SE050's T=1 target. See Testing and CI . Where to go next ¶ Quickstart Wire four signals, write the port, read random bytes from the chip. Hardware Pins, supplies, I2C speed and address, power-down and reset. docs.text: API guide ¶ How to do the common jobs with the driver: bring the chip up, read its state, store data, use keys, send your own APDUs, open a secure channel and handle errors. Every snippet on this page is compiled by the host CI from tests/docs/api_tasks.cpp , with Se standing for se050::Device<MyI2c> . The API reference lists every member. The shape of the API ¶ One Device<Transport> per chip. It owns a T1Session (the link) and an scp03::Session (the optional secure channel), and offers the IoT applet's commands as member functions. Under it, free functions build and parse the bytes, so you can send any command the device object does not cover. OpenSecureChannel() returns Error::NotSupported when a key or the 8-byte host challenge is missing, and Error::Protocol when the card cryptogram does not match (wrong keys). Inside the channel any response without a valid R-MAC returns Error::Authentication and closes the channel; later commands return the same until Scp03().Close() or a new OpenSecureChannel() . The Security model page covers provisioning and the limits of the channel. Handle errors ¶ se050::Error Meaning and what to do Ok Success NotInitialized The port's EnsureInitialized() returned false . Check bus set-up Transport , Timeout An I2C write failed, or a read failed after the retries. Wiring, address, power, ENA; Troubleshooting Crc Blocks kept arriving with a wrong CRC after the retransmissions ( SetMaxRetransmissions() ). Noise, speed, a port that splits writes; recover Sequence The SE050's N(S) is not the expected one. Recover Protocol Bad framing, too many WTX requests or retransmissions, or a typed command answered SW other than 90 00 . Recover; for a status word, send the command with TransmitApdu() to see it BufferTooSmall The answer does not fit your buffer, or the SCP03 scratch is missing. Pass a larger buffer InvalidArgument A null pointer or a length out of range. Fix the call NotSupported SCP03 without keys, or wrap without an open channel. Provision keys Authentication Inside the SCP03 channel, a response without a valid R-MAC; or a command after the channel was lost. The keys are wiped. Treat as tampering; Scp03().Close() or open a new channel After any error below the applet level ( Transport , Timeout , Crc , Sequence , Protocol from framing), the T=1 state of host and chip may differ. Start over: // After any T=1-level error the sequence numbers may disagree with the chip: start over. se050 :: Error recover ( Se & se ) { se . T1 (). ResetSequenceState (); return se . T1 (). ChipWarmReset ( 100 ); } If that fails too, power-cycle the SE050 with HardwareReset() (ENA) and bring it up again. A chip that stretches the clock forever needs a power cycle: see erratum I2C.1 on the Hardware page. T1().RecoverAfterHostReset() at start-up prevents the usual cause, a host reset in the middle of an exchange.

Three layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources From top to bottom. Your application talks to one se050::Device object, whose public commands are listed from inc/se050_device.hpp. Each command builds an APDU, which the T=1 session (inc/se050_t1_session.hpp) frames into blocks with a CRC-16 EDC, chains and acknowledges; when an SCP03 session is open the APDU is wrapped first. The communication interface (se050::I2cTransceiveInterface in inc/se050_i2c_transport_interface.hpp) is a CRTP base. The platform port is the only code you write: the methods listed from that header's requirements. Below it is the SE050 on I2C. How one command reaches the chip ¶ sequenceDiagram participant A as Application participant D as Device participant S as scp03::Session participant T as T1Session participant P as Your port A->>D: GetRandom(32, ...) D->>D: build APDU 80 04 00 49 04 41 02 00 20 00 opt SCP03 channel open D->>S: WrapCommand (C-MAC, C-ENC) end D->>T: ExchangeInformation(APDU) T->>P: I2cWrite(5A PCB LEN APDU CRC) T->>P: I2cRead(3), then I2cRead(LEN + 2) P-->>T: A5 PCB LEN R-APDU CRC T-->>D: R-APDU, CRC checked opt SCP03 channel open D->>S: UnwrapResponse (R-MAC, R-ENC) end D->>D: parse tag 0x41 and SW 90 00 D-->>A: Error::Ok and 32 bytes Design choices ¶ CRTP, not virtual functions. The port is a template parameter: Device<MyI2c> . The compiler sees your methods directly; there is no vtable, no RTTI and nothing to allocate. Code that must work with several port types takes the device as a template parameter too. Caller-owned buffers. Every command takes the output buffer and its capacity, and returns Error::BufferTooSmall rather than truncating. Working buffers are on the stack ( Configuration ); the SCP03 wrap uses a buffer you bind once. Errors are values. Every call returns se050::Error ; nothing throws. A status word other than 90 00 from a typed command becomes Error::Protocol ; TransmitApdu() and the Select*() helpers return the raw R-APDU so you can read the status words yourself. Plaintext unless you provision keys. TransmitApdu() wraps only when Scp03().IsOpen() ; opening the channel needs keys you pass at run time. A channel lost to a bad R-MAC is not replaced by plaintext behind your back: calls fail with Error::Authentication until you close or reopen it. See Security model . One owner. The driver keeps T=1 sequence numbers and the SCP03 counter in the object. It is not thread-safe; give each SE050 one owner task or one mutex around every call. docs.text: Changelog ¶ What changed in each release of the driver. All notable changes to this driver are listed here. The format follows Keep a Changelog and the project uses Semantic Versioning . [Unreleased] ¶ Security ¶ SCP03: a response inside an open channel is never accepted without a verified R-MAC. A response shorter than R-MAC + status word (for example a bare 90 00 injected on the bus) used to pass through unchecked, faking success for status-only commands; it now returns Error::Authentication and closes the channel (GPC Amendment D 6.2.5). SCP03: R-MACs and the card cryptogram are compared in constant time. SCP03: session keys, MAC chaining value and counter are wiped with a non-elidable SecureZero() on Close() , on every failure and in the destructor; AES round keys, CMAC subkeys and handshake intermediates are wiped too. SCP03: after a lost channel the device refuses commands with Error::Authentication until Scp03().Close() or a new channel, instead of silently sending plaintext. Fixed ¶ apdu::BuildCase4Extended() wrote a three-byte Le after an extended Lc; case 4E has a two-byte Le (ISO/IEC 7816-4 5.1). SCP03 wrap read every command as short case 3: it dropped Le from case 2 and 4 commands and sent extended commands without their data. All cases (1, 2, 3, 4, short and extended) are now wrapped, extended commands in extended form, with Le kept. SCP03 erratum JOS.2 (errata sheet 3.13): commands without data now carry an encrypted padding block, so the SE050's counter stays in step; GetVersion() works inside the channel. T=1: a block with a bad EDC is requested again and an R-block NACK from the SE050 makes the host resend its I-block (ISO/IEC 7816-3 11.6.3), up to SetMaxRetransmissions() times. T=1: command blocks are cut at the SE050's IFSC from the ATR ( GetAnswerToReset() ), not always at 254 bytes. CMake: install rules and an exported hf::se050 target, so find_package(hf_se050) works; the package config no longer includes the uninstalled build-settings script. The ESP-IDF component manifest said 0.2.0 while CMake said 0.3.0; both say 0.3.0 and configuring fails if they differ. Added ¶ T1Session::RecoverAfterHostReset() : the start-up read for erratum I2C.1 (errata sheet 3.1.3), then S(RESYNCH). T1Session::SetIfsc() / Ifsc() , SetMaxRetransmissions() / MaxRetransmissions() , t1::RBlockNackPcb() . scp03::ParseCommand() , scp03::WipeChannel() , scp03::kWrapScratchBytesExtended , scp03::Session::Failed() and Abort() , scp03::crypto::SecureZero() , ScopedWipe , ConstantTimeEqual() . Host tests for SCP03 against a card model (tampered R-MAC, status word only, replay, wiping, JOS.2, extended APDUs), T=1 retransmission, IFSC and I2C.1, and an install test ( hf_se050_install ). Host unit tests ( -DHF_SE050_BUILD_TESTS=ON ) against a model of the SE050's T=1 over I2C target, and a CI workflow that runs them with GCC and Clang. Changed ¶ Documentation moved to the HardFOC MkDocs platform: new page set (quickstart, hardware, architecture, T=1 over I2C, security model, API guide, configuration, porting, testing), code snippets compiled by the host build from tests/docs/ , Doxygen under /api/ , versioned with mike. The Jekyll site files and the doxygen-awesome submodule are gone. Shorter, more precise example descriptions in examples/esp32/app_config.yml . Breaking changes ¶ New enumerator Error::Authentication . A switch over se050::Error without default needs a case for it. An R-MAC failure returns Error::Authentication instead of Error::Protocol , and so does any response inside the channel without an R-MAC, including error status words the SE050 sends unprotected. After it, TransmitApdu() and every command fail with Error::Authentication until Scp03().Close() or a new channel (previously the device fell back to plaintext). A T=1 error inside the channel now also closes it. Wrapped commands are longer: every command carries at least one encrypted block (JOS.2), and commands with an Le now send it. Commands over 255 bytes of data need a wrap buffer of kWrapScratchBytesExtended (they used to be sent malformed). scp03::Session is no longer copyable (session keys are never duplicated), so neither is Device . A block with a bad EDC no longer ends the exchange with Error::Crc at once; it is retried first. 0.3.0 (version in the build settings; not tagged) ¶ CRTP I2C transport, T=1 over I2C session (CRC, chaining, WTX, resynchronisation), ATR parser, APDU and TLV helpers, IoT applet commands for management, binary objects, EC keys, ECDSA, AES and RFC 3394 unwrap. Platform SCP03: handshake, wrap and unwrap of short APDUs, Card Manager SELECT and PUT KEY , with no compiled-in keys. ESP-IDF port and seven ESP32 examples, from bring-up to an IoT lifecycle.

docs.text: Configuration ¶ Every setting the driver has: T=1 timing, the I2C address and ENA in your port, the ESP32 reference port's options, and the memory the driver uses. T=1 timing ¶ auto & t1 = se . T1 (); t1 . SetInterFrameDelayMs ( 3 ); // wait after each block write before the first read (default 2 ms) t1 . SetReadRetries ( 10 ); // re-read a NACKed or timed-out read this many times (default 6) t1 . SetReadRetryDelayMs ( 2 ); // between those reads (default 2 ms) t1 . SetMaxWtxRequests ( 16 ); // S(WTX) requests accepted in one exchange (default 8) Setter Default Raise it when SetInterFrameDelayMs(ms) 2 ms The first read after a write keeps failing; some boards need 3 ms SetReadRetries(n) 6 The chip NACKs for longer than retries × delay (slow configurations, low bus speed) SetReadRetryDelayMs(ms) 2 ms Same; together with retries it bounds how long a read waits SetMaxWtxRequests(n) 8 Long operations (RSA, key generation) end in Error::Protocol after many WTX requests SetMaxRetransmissions(n) 3 A noisy bus ends exchanges in Error::Crc although single blocks get through SetIfsc(n) 254 Never by hand in normal use: GetAnswerToReset() sets it from the SE050's ATR Each setter has a getter ( InterFrameDelayMs() , ReadRetries() , ReadRetryDelayMs() , MaxWtxRequests() , MaxRetransmissions() , Ifsc() ). The settings live in the T1Session of each device object and apply to every later exchange. Address and ENA ¶ The I2C address and the ENA pin belong to your port, not the driver. The port on the Porting page takes both in its constructor: MyI2c i2c_default ; // 0x48, ENA not wired MyI2c i2c_on_board ( 0x48 , /*ena_gpio=*/ 21 ); // ENA wired to GPIO 21 se050::kDefaultI2cAddress7 is 0x48 , the SE050's default target address. ESP32 reference port ¶ The examples' port, hf_se050_examples::HfSe050EspIdfI2c , takes a Se050EspI2cConfig : Field Default Meaning port I2C_NUM_0 ESP-IDF I2C controller sda , scl GPIO_NUM_47 , GPIO_NUM_48 Pins (ESP32-S3 example wiring) freq_hz 100000 SCL frequency device_address7 0x48 SE050 address reset_gpio GPIO_NUM_NC GPIO wired to ENA, or not connected It uses the ESP-IDF v5 i2c_master driver with the internal pull-ups enabled and a glitch filter of 7 clock cycles; see hf_se050_esp_i2c.hpp . Limits ¶ Constant Value Meaning se050::kMaxApduCommandBytes 892 Largest C-APDU the builders produce se050::kMaxApduResponseBytes 892 Largest R-APDU buffer the commands use se050::t1::kMaxInformationField 254 INF bytes per T=1 block se050::scp03::kWrapScratchBytes 320 Minimum size of the buffer for BindScp03WrapScratch() (short commands) se050::scp03::kWrapScratchBytesExtended 925 Wrap buffer size for any command, extended ones included Buffers and stack ¶ The driver allocates nothing. Commands put their working buffers on the stack of the calling task: Call Largest stack buffers WriteBinary() 892-byte C-APDU, 64-byte response GetRandom() , ReadObject() , EcdsaSign() 892-byte response Any exchange ( T1Session ) Two 259-byte block buffers (send and receive) The deepest call needs about 1.5 kB for these buffers, plus call frames. Data you read goes into buffers you pass, and the SCP03 wrap uses the buffer you bind with BindScp03WrapScratch() , which can live in static memory. Compile-time ¶ There are no configuration macros. se050_version.h , generated at configure time, gives the version ( Installation ).

docs.text: The driver allocates nothing. Commands put their working buffers on the stack of the calling task: Call Largest stack buffers WriteBinary() 892-byte C-APDU, 64-byte response GetRandom() , ReadObject() , EcdsaSign() 892-byte response Any exchange ( T1Session ) Two 259-byte block buffers (send and receive) The deepest call needs about 1.5 kB for these buffers, plus call frames. Data you read goes into buffers you pass, and the SCP03 wrap uses the buffer you bind with BindScp03WrapScratch() , which can live in static memory.

docs.text: Hardware ¶ What to connect between your MCU and an SE050, with which bus settings, and the board-level details that decide whether the chip answers. All values here come from the SE050 datasheet (Rev. 3.8, 18 October 2023) unless a row says otherwise. NXP does not allow its PDFs to be redistributed, so they are linked, not stored in the repository. Pins (HX2QFN20) ¶ Pin Name Use with this driver 9 I2C_SDA I2C data, open drain 10 I2C_SCL I2C clock, input 11 ENA Deep power-down while low 12 VIN I2C pad supply 18 VCC Logic supply 15 VOUT Feeds VCC for deep power-down 19 VSS Ground 3, 16 IO1, IO2 Not used 13, 14 CLK, RST_N Not used 1, 17 LB, LA Not used: to VSS 2, 4-8, 20 n.c. Not connected ENA is referenced to VIN. Tie it to VCC when you do not drive it. VIN also supplies the logic when deep power-down is used; VCC is then fed from VOUT on the board. Without deep power-down, leave VOUT unconnected. IO1 / IO2 carry ISO 7816 or the SE050's own I2C controller (400 kHz) for sensors behind it. CLK / RST_N belong to ISO 7816; RST_N has no effect when only I2C is enabled. LA / LB are the ISO 14443 antenna. Connect the centre pad to ground for heat. Reset and power modes ¶ There is no reset pin for the I2C interface. A board resets the SE050 by power-cycling it, or with ENA: Mode Enter Leave Deep power-down: < 5 µA, state lost ENA low ENA high, then boot Power-down: < 500 µA, state kept "End of APDU session" S-block Falling edge on SDA Deep power-down needs the chip supplied through VIN with VCC fed from VOUT. Wired that way, the port's HardwareReset() can pulse ENA low and high to give a clean start; the reference port holds it low for 2 ms and waits 10 ms after release. With VCC tied straight to the supply, use a load switch on the supply instead. The driver does not send the end-of-session block, so it never enters power-down mode by itself. Keep SDA and SCL high while the SE050 boots At power-up the SE050 picks its interface: it uses I2C only when I2C_SDA and I2C_SCL are both high (its weak internal pull-ups are on). A host that holds the bus low during the SE050's boot leaves it waiting for another interface until the next reset. Bus settings ¶ Setting Value Role I2C target; the host is the controller Address 0x48 (7-bit, 1001000 ), se050::kDefaultI2cAddress7 Speed Up to 3.4 MHz (high-speed mode) with clock stretching; 1 MHz without Clock stretching On by default in configurations A, B, C, D, F, above 600 kHz; off by default on SE050E Pull-ups External, to VIN, sized for the bus speed and capacitance Protocol Smartcard T=1 over I2C, NXP UM11225 ( T=1 over I2C ) A host that cannot handle clock stretching stays below 600 kHz on a configuration with stretching on, or uses a configuration with stretching off, which runs up to 1 MHz. The ESP32 examples run at 100 kHz, which every configuration supports; start there for bring-up. How an exchange looks on the bus ¶ The host writes one complete T=1 block, waits the inter-frame delay, then reads the answer in two parts: the three-byte prologue (NAD, PCB, LEN), then LEN bytes of information and the two-byte CRC. While the SE050 is still working it NACKs its address, and the driver retries the read. sequenceDiagram participant H as Host (driver) participant S as SE050 H->>S: write: 5A PCB LEN [APDU ...] CRC Note over H: inter-frame delay (2 ms) H->>S: read 3 bytes S--xH: NACK (busy) Note over H: retry after 2 ms H->>S: read 3 bytes S-->>H: A5 PCB LEN H->>S: read LEN + 2 bytes S-->>H: [R-APDU ...] CRC A long operation (key generation, RSA) may answer with an S(WTX) request instead; the driver answers it and keeps reading. T=1 over I2C has the block types and the timing settings. Power ¶ Supply Range Notes VIN, VCC 1.62 V to 3.6 V, 1.8 V typical Characterised range. 6 V absolute maximum; above 3.6 V the deep power-down current is not guaranteed Digital inputs −0.3 V to VIN + 0.3 V SDA, SCL and ENA are referenced to VIN Temperature grade (part number digit) Ambient range 1 (standard) −25 °C to 85 °C 2 (extended) −40 °C to 105 °C Run the MCU's I/O at the SE050's VIN, or add a level shifter: the SE050 is not 5 V tolerant within its operating range. Errata that affect the host ¶ From the SE050 errata sheet (Rev. 1.0, 14 October 2020): I2C.1, lock-up on an erroneous APDU sequence. A command written before the previous response was read in full can make the SE050 stretch SCL forever (when clock stretching is on), until it is power-cycled. A host that resets in the middle of an exchange causes exactly this. The driver always reads a response to the end; after a host reset, follow NXP's workaround (3.1.3) and read from the SE050 before the first command: T1().RecoverAfterHostReset() reads any pending answer and resynchronises. Once the bus is locked only a power cycle helps: wire ENA so HardwareReset() can do it. I2C.2, empty frame. An acknowledged address-only frame (START, address, STOP) also makes the SE050 stretch the clock forever. The driver never sends one and Session::TransceiveRaw() rejects a zero-length write. Do not run an I2C bus scan with the SE050 on the bus. I2C.3, lines low at start-up. SDA or SCL low during interface detection triggers a security reset after about 1 s, and repeated events lock the chip. Keep the bus idle high, with pull-ups, whenever the SE050 is powered. I2C.4, edge timing. SCL must change before SDA with a margin: data hold time (50 % to 50 %) at least 8 ns for a falling and 24 ns for a rising SDA edge in fast mode. Check your I2C controller's hold-time setting. JOS.2, SCP03 counter. Inside a platform SCP03 session, a command without command data does not advance the SE050's encryption counter, and the next command fails. The driver applies NXP's workaround (3.13.3): every wrapped command carries encrypted data. See Security model . One host per SE050, one command at a time I2C.1 is why the driver is not thread-safe and must not be shared between tasks without a lock: two commands interleaved on the bus can hang it until a power cycle. Configurations ¶ SE050 is a family of pin-compatible configurations (SE050A, B, C, D, E, F and their variants) that differ in enabled features, pre-provisioned credentials, clock-stretching default and certification. NXP's configurations note AN12436 lists them; check the one on your board before you choose a bus speed, an applet AID or object identifiers. The default AID in se050::applet::kDefaultIoTAppletAid is the Plug & Trust IoT applet's; confirm it for your configuration. Evaluation and example boards ¶ The ESP32 examples run on an ESP32-S3 with the SE050 on I2C port 0. The fields are those of Se050EspI2cConfig ; ENA is not connected by default ( GPIO_NUM_NC ). Signal ESP32-S3 Field SDA 47 sda SCL 48 scl ENA n.c. reset_gpio Bus speed 100 kHz freq_hz Address 0x48 device_address7 The reference port turns on the ESP32's internal pull-ups, which are weak; add external pull-ups for anything but a short bench connection. The configuration is in hf_se050_esp_i2c.hpp . docs.text: Installation ¶ Add the driver to a CMake or ESP-IDF project. It is a header-only C++17 library with no dependencies. Requirements ¶ A C++17 compiler. CI builds with the GCC and Clang of Ubuntu 24.04; the examples with ESP-IDF v5.5. No RTOS, heap or exceptions: every call is noexcept and returns se050::Error (or bool ). About 1.5 kB of stack for the deepest call: an 892-byte APDU buffer and two 259-byte T=1 block buffers live on the stack while a command runs ( Configuration ). Get the source ¶ A git submodule keeps the driver pinned to a version you chose: git submodule add https://github.com/hardfoc/hf-se050-driver.git external/hf-se050-driver git submodule update --init external/hf-se050-driver Only inc/ , cmake/ and CMakeLists.txt are needed to build. The examples have their own submodule ( examples/esp32/scripts ); you do not need it to use the driver. CMake ¶ add_subdirectory ( external/hf-se050-driver ) target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE hf::se050 ) hf::se050 (alias of hf_se050 ) is an INTERFACE target: it carries the include directories, including the generated version header, and requires C++17 ( cxx_std_17 ). Option Default Effect HF_SE050_ENABLE_WARNINGS OFF -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic on targets that link hf::se050 HF_SE050_BUILD_TESTS OFF Builds the host unit tests in tests/ ( Testing and CI ) To use an installed copy instead, install the driver and find it as a package: cmake -S hf-se050-driver -B build && cmake --install build --prefix /opt/hf find_package ( hf_se050 0.3 REQUIRED CONFIG ) # CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/opt/hf target_link_libraries ( app PRIVATE hf::se050 ) The headers and se050_version.h install under include/hf_se050 , the package files under lib/cmake/hf_se050 . The CMake version, HF_SE050_VERSION and the ESP-IDF component manifest carry the same version; configuring fails if they differ. ESP-IDF ¶ The ESP-IDF component wrapper is examples/esp32/components/hf_se050/ . Copy that folder into your project's components/ (or point EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS at it) and set the HF_SE050_ROOT cache variable to the driver checkout; the wrapper stops with a clear message when the path is wrong. Your component then declares REQUIRES hf_se050 . The wrapper itself requires driver and freertos , for the ESP-IDF port in the examples. How the build is organised ¶ Layer File Role Settings cmake/hf_se050_build_settings.cmake Include directories, version, version header: the single source of truth Library CMakeLists.txt INTERFACE target for host builds and CI ESP-IDF examples/esp32/components/hf_se050/CMakeLists.txt IDF component wrapper over the same settings The version is set once in the settings file and written into se050_version.h in the build tree at configure time: Macro Value HF_SE050_VERSION_MAJOR , _MINOR , _PATCH 0 , 3 , 0 HF_SE050_VERSION_STRING "0.3.0" Headers ¶ Include se050_device.hpp for the device object, or se050_driver.hpp for everything (T=1, APDU, TLV, ATR, commands, SCP03, RFC 3394). The API reference lists every header. Next ¶ Quickstart wires the chip and reads random bytes; Porting writes the I2C interface for your MCU.

docs.text: Porting ¶ Run the driver on a new MCU by writing one class: the I2C interface. The driver never calls your SDK directly. It calls six methods on a class you derive from se050::I2cTransceiveInterface<Self> (in inc/se050_i2c_transport_interface.hpp ). The base class uses CRTP: the calls are resolved at compile time, so there are no virtual functions, no vtable and nothing to allocate. Three layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources From top to bottom. Your application talks to one se050::Device object, whose public commands are listed from inc/se050_device.hpp. Each command builds an APDU, which the T=1 session (inc/se050_t1_session.hpp) frames into blocks with a CRC-16 EDC, chains and acknowledges; when an SCP03 session is open the APDU is wrapped first. The communication interface (se050::I2cTransceiveInterface in inc/se050_i2c_transport_interface.hpp) is a CRTP base. The platform port is the only code you write: the methods listed from that header's requirements. Below it is the SE050 on I2C. Drawn from: inc/se050_device.hpp Device commands ; inc/se050_t1_session.hpp T1Session ; inc/se050_i2c_transport_interface.hpp Derived requirements ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/driver-layers.py . What you implement ¶ Method Contract bool EnsureInitialized() Return true once the bus is ready. Called before every exchange: make it cheap after the first call Error I2cWrite(tx, tx_len, timeout_ms) One I2C write of exactly tx_len bytes to the SE050's address: START, address + W, the bytes, STOP. tx_len is never 0 Error I2cRead(rx, rx_len, timeout_ms) One I2C read of exactly rx_len bytes. Return Transport or Timeout on a NACK: the driver retries those two Error Transceive(tx, tx_len, rx, rx_cap, rx_len_out, timeout_ms) A write then a read, for Device::TransceiveRaw() during bring-up only; T=1 does not use it Error HardwareReset() Power-cycle the SE050 (ENA low, then high) if your board can; return Ok if it cannot void delay_ms_impl(ms) Block for at least ms milliseconds (an RTOS delay is fine) All methods are noexcept . Return Error::Ok on success; any other value aborts the exchange (after retries, for reads). Never zero-length. se050 :: Error I2cWrite ( const std :: uint8_t * tx , std :: size_t tx_len , std :: uint32_t timeout_ms ) noexcept { if ( tx == nullptr || tx_len == 0U ) { return se050 :: Error :: InvalidArgument ; } return platform_i2c_write ( addr7_ , tx , tx_len , timeout_ms ) ? se050 :: Error :: Ok : se050 :: Error :: Transport ; } // Exactly rx_len bytes in one I2C read. A NACK (the SE050 is still busy) is Transport: the driver // retries. se050 :: Error I2cRead ( std :: uint8_t * rx , std :: size_t rx_len , std :: uint32_t timeout_ms ) noexcept { if ( rx == nullptr || rx_len == 0U ) { return se050 :: Error :: InvalidArgument ; } return platform_i2c_read ( addr7_ , rx , rx_len , timeout_ms ) ? se050 :: Error :: Ok : se050 :: Error :: Transport ; } // Bring-up helper only (Device::TransceiveRaw); T=1 uses I2cWrite / I2cRead. se050 :: Error Transceive ( const std :: uint8_t * tx , std :: size_t tx_len , std :: uint8_t * rx , std :: size_t rx_cap , std :: size_t * rx_len_out , std :: uint32_t timeout_ms ) noexcept { * rx_len_out = 0 ; se050 :: Error e = I2cWrite ( tx , tx_len , timeout_ms ); if ( e != se050 :: Error :: Ok || rx == nullptr || rx_cap == 0U ) { return e ; } delay_ms_impl ( 2 ); e = I2cRead ( rx , rx_cap , timeout_ms ); if ( e == se050 :: Error :: Ok ) { * rx_len_out = rx_cap ; } return e ; } // Power-cycle through ENA (deep power-down while low). An address-only frame can hang the SE050 (erratum I2C.2, see Hardware ). Report NACKs as Transport or Timeout . The SE050 NACKs reads while it works; the driver polls through them. Pull-ups and idle-high lines before the SE050 powers up ( Hardware ). On HardFOC boards the SE050 is used through Se050Handler in hf-core : it implements this interface over the HAL's BaseI2c and an optional BaseGpio for the reset line (wire it to ENA), adds a mutex and owns the Device . Build it with HF_CORE_ENABLE_SE050 . Check your port ¶ Build it: the port on this page is compiled by the host CI from tests/docs/ , with every driver class instantiated over it. SelectDefaultIoTApplet() answering 90 00 , then GetRandom(32, ...) : APDUs work end to end. Run the se050_smoke_example logic on your board: version, random and free memory. docs.text: Security model ¶ What the SE050 and this driver protect, what they do not, how to provision keys, and how the common device security flows map onto the driver's calls. This page is engineering guidance, not a certification argument. For a product, read NXP's use and security guidelines AN12514 and your configuration's entry in AN12436 alongside it. What the SE050 gives you ¶ Keys that do not leave the chip. GenerateEcKeyPair() creates the private key inside the SE050. The host can read the public key and ask for signatures; it cannot read the private key. Signing and verification on chip. EcdsaSign() and EcdsaVerify() take a digest you computed; the signature is ASN.1 DER. Secure storage. Binary objects and AES keys in up to 50 kB of user flash, addressed by a 4-byte object identifier. A true random number generator. GetRandom() ; NIST SP800-90B TRNG and SP800-90A DRBG. A certified environment. Common Criteria EAL 6+ for hardware and OS (datasheet); FIPS 140-2 level 3 only on specific product types. Bus protection. GlobalPlatform SCP03 between host and chip, which this driver implements. What this driver does, and does not ¶ The driver does: Transport: T=1 over I2C with CRC. APDUs are plaintext by default. Platform SCP03: INITIALIZE UPDATE and EXTERNAL AUTHENTICATE at security level 0x33 (C-MAC, C-ENC, R-MAC, R-ENC), wrap and unwrap of short and extended APDUs, and BuildPutKey() to replace the key set. docs.text: T=1 over I2C ¶ How the driver carries APDUs to the SE050: the ISO/IEC 7816-3 T=1 block protocol, as NXP adapts it to I2C in UM11225, and what T1Session does at each step. Blocks ¶ Every exchange is a sequence of blocks. The host writes a block in one I2C write; the SE050's answer is read in two I2C reads, the prologue first. Field Bytes Content NAD 1 0x5A host to SE050, 0xA5 SE050 to host PCB 1 Block type and sequence bits, below LEN 1 Length of INF, 0 to 254 INF LEN APDU bytes, or an S-block's parameter EDC 2 CRC-16 over NAD to INF, LSB first The constants are t1::kNadHostToSe , t1::kNadSeToHost and t1::kMaxInformationField . The EDC is CRC-16/X-25: reflected polynomial 0x8408 , initial value 0xFFFF , final XOR 0xFFFF (check value 0x906E for "123456789" , tested in tests/test_t1.cpp ). A block that fails the check is asked for again ( Error recovery ); after the retransmission limit the exchange fails with Error::Crc . Block types ¶ PCB Block and what the driver does with it 0x00 , 0x40 I-block, N(S) = 0 or 1; +0x20 sets M (more follows). APDU data both ways: t1::IBlockPcb(ns, more) 0x80 , 0x90 R-block, N(R) = 0 or 1 (error code in the low bits). Acknowledges a chained block ( t1::RBlockAckPcb(nr) ), or asks for a block again ( t1::RBlockNackPcb(nr, err) ) 0xC0 / 0xE0 S(RESYNCH) request / response. The SE050 asks; the driver resets its sequence numbers and answers 0xC3 / 0xE3 S(WTX) request / response. The SE050 needs more time; the driver echoes the INF and keeps waiting 0xC6 / 0xE6 S-block reset request / response. ChipWarmReset() : resets the T=1 state on both sides 0xC7 / 0xE7 S(GET ATR) request / response. GetAnswerToReset() returns the profile bytes Sequence numbers and chaining ¶ The host and the SE050 each keep a one-bit send sequence number, N(S), which alternates with every I-block they send. T1Session keeps both and checks the SE050's: an I-block with the wrong N(S) is Error::Sequence . An APDU longer than the SE050's IFSC (254 bytes unless its ATR says less) is split. Every block but the last has the M bit set, and the SE050 acknowledges each with an R-block before the host sends the next. Long responses come back the same way, and the driver acknowledges each chained block with an R-block carrying N(R). sequenceDiagram participant H as Host participant S as SE050 H->>S: I(0, M) 254 bytes S-->>H: R(1) H->>S: I(1) 46 bytes S-->>H: S(WTX request) H->>S: S(WTX response) S-->>H: I(0, M) first part of the response H->>S: R(1) S-->>H: I(1) last part, ends with SW1 SW2 Error recovery ¶ T1Session follows the error rules of ISO/IEC 7816-3 section 11.6.3: A block from the SE050 with a bad EDC is answered with an R-block carrying the expected N(R) and the EDC error code; the SE050 sends the block again. An R-block from the SE050 whose N(R) equals the N(S) of the host's last I-block means the SE050 did not accept it; the host sends that I-block again, inside a chain or after the last block. Each exchange allows SetMaxRetransmissions() (default 3) of these; after that it fails with Error::Crc or Error::Protocol . After an error that ends an exchange the two sides may disagree about the sequence numbers. Call ResetSequenceState() and ChipWarmReset() before the next command ( API guide ). After a host reset ¶ If the MCU resets in the middle of an exchange, the SE050 may still hold an answer, and writing a new command before reading it can lock the bus until the SE050 is power-cycled (erratum I2C.1). Call RecoverAfterHostReset() once at start-up, before the first command: it reads and discards any pending block, then sends S(RESYNCH request) so both sides start from N(S) = 0. When nothing is pending, the read is simply NACKed until the read retries run out. Timing ¶ Setting Default Meaning SetInterFrameDelayMs() 2 ms Wait after every block write before the first read SetReadRetries() 6 Re-reads after a read that returned Transport or Timeout (the SE050 NACKs while busy) SetReadRetryDelayMs() 2 ms Wait between those re-reads SetMaxWtxRequests() 8 S(WTX) requests accepted in one exchange before giving up with Error::Protocol SetMaxRetransmissions() 3 Blocks requested or sent again in one exchange ( Error recovery ) SetIfsc() 254 Largest INF per command block; GetAnswerToReset() sets it from the ATR timeout_ms argument per call Passed to every I2cWrite() / I2cRead() of the exchange With the defaults, a read gives up after 7 attempts, 12 ms of waiting plus the I2C time. Commands that take longer (EC key generation, RSA) are covered by the SE050's WTX requests, not by the retries. Configuration shows how to change the settings. The ATR ¶ GetAnswerToReset() returns the SE050's profile bytes; se050::atr::Parse() decodes them into atr::Profile : protocol version, vendor ID, block waiting time ( bwt ), IFSC, maximum I2C clock ( max_i2c_khz ), minimum polling time, guard time ( segt_us ), wake-up time and the historical bytes. GetAnswerToReset() takes the IFSC from the profile, so later commands are split at the SE050's block size. The timing settings above are not adapted: log the profile at bring-up and set them from it if your configuration differs. What the driver does not use ¶ The driver implements the blocks above. It does not send S(IFS) to change the block size, S(ABORT), the end-of-APDU-session request that puts the SE050 into power-down mode, or the interface soft reset.

docs.text: GetAnswerToReset() returns the SE050's profile bytes; se050::atr::Parse() decodes them into atr::Profile : protocol version, vendor ID, block waiting time ( bwt ), IFSC, maximum I2C clock ( max_i2c_khz ), minimum polling time, guard time ( segt_us ), wake-up time and the historical bytes. GetAnswerToReset() takes the IFSC from the profile, so later commands are split at the SE050's block size. The timing settings above are not adapted: log the profile at bring-up and set them from it if your configuration differs.

docs.text: Testing and CI ¶ How the driver is checked: host unit tests against a model of the SE050's T=1 target, compiled documentation, ESP32 builds and static analysis, on every pull request. docs.text: Troubleshooting ¶ Symptoms you may see while bringing up an SE050, their causes and the fix for each, cheapest check first. Start with the se050::Error of the first call that fails. Transport and Timeout point at the bus, Crc , Sequence and framing Protocol at the link, and a status word other than 90 00 at the applet or its configuration. Nothing answers ¶ Symptom Cause and fix Every call returns Transport Wrong address, no pull-ups, no supply, ENA low. Fix: address 0x48, external pull-ups to VIN, VIN and VCC 1.62 V to 3.6 V, ENA high (or tied to VCC) NotInitialized The port's EnsureInitialized() returns false . Fix: the I2C controller or GPIO set-up in your port Worked, then the bus is stuck low on SCL The SE050 is stretching the clock forever: a command was sent before the previous response was read (erratum I2C.1), or an address-only frame reached it (I2C.2). Fix: power-cycle the SE050 (ENA or supply). Remove bus scans; give the chip one owner; after an MCU reset, power-cycle it or call T1().RecoverAfterHostReset() before the first command Answers only after a power cycle of the whole board The bus was low while the SE050 booted, so it did not select I2C (erratum I2C.3). Fix: keep SDA and SCL high from power-up; power the MCU's I/O first HardwareReset() has no effect ENA not wired, or VCC tied to the supply instead of VOUT. Fix: deep power-down needs VIN supply with VCC fed from VOUT ( Hardware ) The link fails ¶ Symptom Cause and fix Crc on most exchanges Noise, a bus too fast for its pull-ups, a port that splits a block into several writes. Fix: drop to 100 kHz, stronger pull-ups, one I2C write per block Timeout or Transport after long commands The read gave up while the chip was still busy. Fix: raise SetReadRetries() or SetReadRetryDelayMs() ( Configuration ) Protocol after key generation or RSA More WTX requests than SetMaxWtxRequests() allows. Fix: raise it Sequence , or Protocol on the next command after an error Host and chip disagree on N(S). Fix: ResetSequenceState() then ChipWarmReset() ( API guide ) Clock stretching above 600 kHz breaks the MCU's controller Configurations A, B, C, D, F stretch by default above 600 kHz. Fix: stay below 600 kHz, or use a configuration with stretching off (up to 1 MHz) The applet says no ¶ Status word Meaning and likely cause 6A 82 on SELECT File or application not found: Wrong AID for your configuration; check AN12436 69 85 Conditions of use not satisfied: The object exists with another type (an AES key written as a binary file), or a policy forbids it 69 82 Security status not satisfied: The command needs an authenticated session or SCP03 on this configuration 6A 80 Wrong data: A malformed TLV; check the identifier and lengths 6D 00 Instruction not supported: The command is not in your applet version ( GetVersion() ) Typed commands turn any of these into Error::Protocol . To see the status word, send the same command with TransmitApdu() and read the last two bytes. SCP03 ¶ Symptom Cause and fix OpenSecureChannel() returns NotSupported A key or the host challenge is missing or the wrong length. Fix: 16-byte ENC and MAC keys, 8-byte challenge OpenSecureChannel() returns Protocol The card cryptogram does not match: the keys are wrong, or the key version. Fix: keys and key version ( 0x0B ) of your configuration or your provisioning TransmitApdu() returns BufferTooSmall while the channel is open No wrap buffer bound, or one too small for the command. Fix: BindScp03WrapScratch() with scp03::kWrapScratchBytes (320 bytes), or kWrapScratchBytesExtended for commands over 255 data bytes Every call returns Authentication A response failed its R-MAC (or had none), or a T=1 error broke an exchange inside the channel; the channel is closed and its keys wiped. Fix: treat as tampering or a wiring fault; Scp03().Close() , or open a new channel Build ¶ Symptom Cause and fix APP_TYPE not defined in an example build CMake run directly. Fix: build through examples/esp32/scripts/build_app.sh , or pass -DAPP_TYPE=... scripts/ missing Submodule not initialised. Fix: git submodule update --init examples/esp32/scripts se050_version.h not found Including the driver without its CMake target. Fix: link hf::se050 , or use the ESP-IDF component
